reviews.review:
[i]Interior Tales[/i] is a cozy, chill sim game where you decorate interiors for clients with no timers or frustrations. Unlock cool new decor as you complete jobs! 

[h3][u]Gamplay & Settings[/u][/h3]

Settings & extras include; resolution & display options, tooltips on or off, the ability to invert your mouse controls, the ability to change keybinds, and audio controls. 

The gameplay is very similar to others in the genre such as MakeRoom or Small Spaces. There is a tutorial that will get you familiar with the mechanics and have you designing in no time. You will take on jobs from various clients that have specific items or colours they want in their designs. 

[u]Tips N Tricks[/u]

⭐ I could not find out why I was not achieving stars for jobs, turns out you need to SCROLL down the list of objectives (I did not see there was more to do) 

⭐ You are not able to get 3 stars on purpose for some jobs as you need to go back to them at a later time to finish them.

⭐ Look around the map for collectables! They are added to your inventory and can be used or sold. 

⭐ You can filter jobs by theme, which makes it easier to find items specific to that job. You can also filter by style or price. Some jobs will require you to have objects that fall into specific categories. 

⭐The game auto-saves so just make sure to continue or load your game when you reopen it. If you hit a new game do not worry as you can have 3 saved games and can backtrack if you have to on the main menu. 

[h3][u]Overall Experience[/u][/h3]

I don’t mind the graphics being more simplified or the design layouts limited to being more modular. I love the challenge of meeting all the client’s objectives and earning a perfect score (I also love unlocking more items or finding secret items on each map). The game has quite a bit of content for the price you pay and offers many hours of fun if you enjoy the job aspect of these types of games. You do get to eventually decorate your own spaces that you earn by completing challenges in the game. 

Some jobs have to be revisited at a later time to finish while others are locked until you complete other jobs beforehand so you cannot just design one job at a time and move forward. In this game progress is not linear. 

I find this game actually pretty relaxing, the music is laid back but you can play your own tunes as well while designing. There are no time limits with lots of gameplay and some achievements to earn for those that love them too. ✨
